institution.name: Church of Bretonnia
institution.model: fictional institution inspired structurally by the medieval Catholic Church
civilizational_role: provides religious and cultural cohesion across the politically fragmented Bretonnian Lands
preserves shared rites, institutions, learning, moral language, and customs across borders
acts as one of the few genuinely trans-regional institutions in Bretonnian civilization
limitations: prone to interpret dragons through inherited categories of danger, paganism, or disorder

dragon_conflict.initial_position: The Church is deeply suspicious of dragons and regards them as symbols or creatures associated with dangerous older traditions outside accepted religious understanding.
dragon_conflict.narrative_symbolism: The Church's distrust of dragons represents the conservative side of an institution that is culturally important and civilizationally cohesive but can resist new realities.
dragon_conflict.development: The Dragon Rider Order demonstrates through conduct and sacrifice that the dragons are loyal defenders of people and political order rather than forces of evil.
dragon_conflict.resolution: The Church reforms its position positively and publicly accepts the dragons after their decisive contribution to resolving the story's political and military crisis.
dragon_conflict.theme: Tradition and institutions can preserve civilization while still needing reform when reality disproves inherited assumptions.
